title: Losing the name before the box: measuring and repairing what narrow fine-tuning costs a detector outside its deployment vocabulary
abstract: arXiv:2609.36426v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: A detector pretrained on a broad corpus is fine-tuned on a narrow domain, its in-domain accuracy improves, and it ships. We ask what happens meanwhile to its coverage of objects the vocabulary never names, which in obstacle detection and inspection carry the risk. No in-domain test set holds an example of one. We give a longitudinal protocol: one pretrained checkpoint against its own fine-tuned descendants. It tracks held-out top-$K$ proposal coverage $C_\tau$: of categories pretraining covered and the vocabulary omits, the share of boxes a detector's top $K$ regions still cover. The quantity is the open-world proposal literature's; the longitudinal reading is not. $C_\tau$ falls while in-domain accuracy rises, on four architectures and three domains, by $5.12$ to $63.35$ points on boxes above $1024$ px$^2$. No in-domain number identifies the fall, and neither does detection average precision, which charges a missed and a misnamed box

translated_title: 先丢名字，后丢框：测量并修复窄域微调使检测器在部署词表之外付出的代价
translated_abstract: 在广泛语料库上预训练的检测器在窄域数据上微调后，其域内准确率提升，随后便被部署上线。我们追问：在此过程中，检测器对词表从未命名过的物体的覆盖能力发生了什么——在障碍物检测与巡检任务中，恰恰是这些物体携带着风险。而任何域内测试集中都不会包含这类物体的样本。我们提出一个纵向评测协议：将同一个预训练检查点与其自身的各个微调后代进行对比。该协议追踪留出集上的top-K提案覆盖率 $C_\tau$：即在预训练覆盖过而部署词表遗漏的类别中，检测器top K候选区域仍然覆盖到的边界框所占比例。这一量度本身来自开放世界提案文献，但对它进行纵向解读是本文的新贡献。在四种架构和三个领域上，当域内准确率上升时，$C_\tau$ 下降了5.12至63.35个点（针对面积大于1024 px²的框）。没有任何域内指标能揭示这种下降，检测平均精度（AP）也不能——因为AP对漏检的框和被错误命名的框一视同仁。
tldr: 本文提出一种纵向评测协议，通过追踪top-K提案覆盖率 $C_\tau$，首次量化揭示了窄域微调在提升域内准确率的同时，会使检测器对部署词表之外类别的覆盖大幅下降（在四种架构和三个领域上损失5.12至63.35个点），且这一损失是域内指标和检测AP都无法察觉的。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces a longitudinal evaluation protocol that tracks held-out top-K proposal coverage $C_\tau$, revealing for the first time that narrow fine-tuning severely erodes a detector's coverage of out-of-vocabulary object classes (by 5.12 to 63.35 points across four architectures and three domains) even as in-domain accuracy improves—a loss invisible to both in-domain metrics and detection AP.
